subject: SDK environment handoff + structured-output pilot — next steps & artifacts
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@brightwell.health>; Samir Rao <samir@brightwell.health>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SDK environment handoff + structured-output pilot — next steps & artifacts

Hi Alice / Samir —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps to get a small sandbox pilot running locally (Python + TS) so your infra team can validate auth, routing, and structured output/tool-calling behavior within Brightwell's network constraints.

Key takeaways:
- Goal: 2-week sandbox to validate SDK auth flows (API key + mutual TLS option), streaming structured outputs (tool calling), and embeddings-based reranking for clinical note search.
- Success criteria: local sample apps boot in <15min, end-to-end tool-calling sample executes against a mock EHR app, embeddings rerank improves recall on the provided test set by +10%.
- Constraints: Brightwell requires KMS-backed keys and audit log capture; on-prem connectivity only (no public webhook callbacks).

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) Share concise artifacts: SDK Quickstart PDF, a dev-environment checklist, and a filled security questionnaire (attached).
2) Rafael + Karthik to provide a 30-min runbook walkthrough (live screen share) and a sandbox repo link (Python + TS sample apps).
3) Brightwell to confirm preferred auth mode (API key rotation via KMS or mTLS) and provide a contact for infra to open a port for outbound calls to our private control plane.

If that matches your expectations, I’ll schedule the runbook session for early next week and drop the sandbox repo link.

Attachments: redwood_sdk_quickstart.pdf (PDF), dev-environment-checklist.md (MD)

Thanks —
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

---
(Inline sample snippet — Python quickstart to validate auth)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<API_KEY_FROM_KMS>")
resp = client.chat.generate(model="redwood-1-s", input="Describe structured output example")
print(resp.structured_output)

(Inline note: TypeScript sample in repo demonstrates tool-calling using the .tools.invoke API and a local mock EHR endpoint.)

From: Alice Park <alice@brightwell.health>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@brightwell.health>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDK environment handoff + structured-output pilot — next steps & artifacts

Thanks Rafael — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side:

- Auth: we prefer KMS-backed API keys for now; would like to avoid mTLS unless necessary. Our security team will want an overview of rotation/cleanup policy.
- Network: we can allow outbound TLS to the control plane IP range you provide; no inbound callbacks.
- Data: test corpus attached (small clinical notes sample) — we’ll use that for embeddings/rerank validation.

Can you make sure the sample app has an option to run entirely locally (no external callbacks) and write logs to stdout so our SI team can capture them? Also please include a mock tool definition that demonstrates structured output -> tool invocation mapping so we can validate the parsing behavior.

I’m attaching Brightwell_Security_Questions_V2.xlsx (answers are partial; security will follow up with specifics).

We can take the runbook demo on Monday 2027-07-19 at 10:00 PT if that works for your schedule.

Best,
Alice
Director, Integrations | Brightwell Health
alice@brightwell.health

Folks —

Quick internal plan before the Monday demo:

Tasks:
- Rafael: finalize the sandbox repo with two toggles: "local-only" and "control-plane-mode" (so Brightwell can exercise both). Include a mock EHR tool that accepts a structured payload (JSON schema) and returns a deterministic response. Add a README that shows how to run the embeddings pipeline locally with faiss. (ETA: EOD Friday)
- Marissa: prepare an abbreviated commercial summary (license, trial seats, expected usage profile, and a preliminary pricing slide) to send after the demo.
- Stephanie: prep a 10-slide runbook demo (auth, routing, logs, fallbacks) and a short checklist to share at the start of the session.

Repo link (private): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4d-sdk-onramp — I’ll copy the sandbox repo there once Rafael pushes.

Rafael — call out any infra or env assumptions in the README. Specifically:
- Python sample tested on 3.10; TS sample tested on Node 18 LTS.
- Dev checklist includes KMS key setup, bastion for private NAT, and local FAISS index instructions.

Karthik

Monday 10:00 PT works for us. A few ask items before the session so our infra folks can block time:
- Please provide the control plane outbound IP CIDR and the TLS root CA you publish so we can add an egress rule.
- Can the Python sample include a toggle to write structured output to a local file instead of attempting callbacks? Our compliance team will run the sample and verify parsing.
- Please confirm that embeddings indexing includes a small script to produce and persist FAISS indices and that the TS sample includes a reranker call with the same index.

If you can drop the sandbox link and the IP/CAs into the Drive folder you listed, I’ll ask our infra lead to check egress rules tomorrow.
